title: User data, instance metadata and IMDSv2

videos.script: An instance boots from an image that a thousand other instances share. {{boot}} So how does it find out which one it is? Its own id, its zone, the role it was given. And who tells it what to install on the first boot? This lesson answers both, and then deals with the risk hidden in the answer. {{userdata}} First, user data. You hand EC2 a script at launch. EC2 stores it and never runs it. A program inside the image fetches it and runs it, once, on the first boot. You will launch with one and read it back, and see why it is no place for a password. {{metadata}} Then the metadata service. It lives at one address that only the instance can reach, and it answers questions about that instance. One of its answers is a set of keys for the instance's role. {{ssrf}} That is the risk. A web application tricked into fetching that address hands the keys to whoever tricked it. In 2019 that cost one bank the records of about a hundred million people. {{token}} IMDSv2 is the fix. A token comes first, from a request a tricked application cannot easily send. You will watch the command line ask for one on its own. {{enforce}} Last, making the token required. On one instance, on a launch template, on a whole account, and in a policy nobody can forget. moto stands in for the service, and it checks none of it. The lesson says exactly where.
